'''Ilka Agricola''' (born 8 August 1973 in [[The Hague]])<ref name="cv">[http://www.mathematik.uni-marburg.de/~agricola/cv.html Curriculum vitae], retrieved 1 January 2017.</ref> is a German mathematician specialising in [[differential geometry]] and its applications in [[mathematical physics]]. She is the dean of mathematics and computer science at [[Marburg University]], where she has also been responsible for making the university's collection of mathematical models public.<ref>{{citation|newspaper=[[Oberhessische Presse]]|language=German|url=http://www.op-marburg.de/UNIversum/Unsere-Wissenschaftler/Vom-Affensattel-zum-Storchenschnabel|title=Vom Affensattel zum Storchenschnabel|date=11 January 2011|first=Manfred|last=Hitzeroth|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=2 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170102080609/http://www.op-marburg.de/UNIversum/Unsere-Wissenschaftler/Vom-Affensattel-zum-Storchenschnabel|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Life and work==
Agricola studied [[physics]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]] and [[LMU Munich]] from 1991 to 1996.<ref name="cv"/> After a guest stay at [[Rutgers University]] in [[New Jersey]] (United States) that lasted until the end of 1997 she went to the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]], where in 2000 she earned a mathematics doctorate under {{ill|Thomas Friedrich (mathematican)|lt=Thomas Friedrich|de|Thomas Friedrich (Mathematiker)}}.<ref name="mathtree">{{mathgenealogy|id=89246}}</ref>

From 2003 to 2008, she led one of the [[Volkswagen Foundation]] funded research groups at the Humboldt University of Berlin in the field of special geometries in [[mathematical physics]]. From 2004 to 2008, she was a [[project manager]] in the priority program for [[string theory]] at the [[German Research Foundation]] and the Collaborative Research Center 1080. Agricola took the [[Habilitation]] in 2004 at the [[University of Greifswald]] in mathematics. In 2008, she was appointed full professor at [[Marburg University]]. From November 2014 until October 2018, she has been Dean of the Department of Mathematics and [[Computer Science]]. She was president of the [[German Mathematical Society]] from 2021 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathematik.de/dmv-blog/2756-p-wahlen-2020|title = Die neuen Präsidiumsmitglieder stehen fest}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10455/updates/18053032|title = Editor-in-Chief Ilka Agricola elected President of the German Mathematical Society (DMV)}}</ref>

Agricola is Editor-in-Chief of two [[academic journal]]s in mathematics published by [[Springer Science+Business Media]], [https://www.springer.com/journal/10455 ''Annals of Global Analysis and Geometry''] (since 2015) and [https://www.springer.com/journal/591 ''Mathematische Semesterberichte''] (since 2021). She is
an editor of the journal ''Communications in Mathematics'' published by [[De Gruyter]].<ref name="journal">[https://www.degruyter.com/view/j/cm ''Communications in Mathematics''], publisher home page, retrieved 1 January 2017.</ref>

As of September 2025, Agricola is chair of the Committee on Publishing of the International Mathematical Union.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://retractionwatch.com/2025/09/24/math-has-publication-fraud-too/|title = Math has publication fraud too}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2003, Ilka Agricola received the Medal of Honor of [[Charles University]] in Prague.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.uni-marburg.de/fb12/pressespiegel_dateien/opagricola.pdf|title=Mit Gauß unter den Weihnachtsbaum|newspaper=[[Oberhessische Presse]]|language=German|date=20 December 2013|first=Tim|last=Gabel}}.</ref> In 2016, she was awarded the {{ill|Ars legendi faculty prize|de|Ars legendi-Preis für exzellente Hochschullehre}} of the [[Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft]] and [[German Rectors' Conference]] for excellence in teaching mathematics.<ref>{{citation|url=https://wissenschaft.hessen.de/presse/pressemitteilung/lehrende-aus-giessen-und-marburg-erhalten-ars-legendi-fakultaetenpreis|title=Lehrende aus Gießen und Marburg erhalten Ars legendi-Fakultätenpreis|language=German|publisher=[[Hessian Ministry for Science and the Arts]]|date=11 April 2016|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=2 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170102203349/https://wissenschaft.hessen.de/presse/pressemitteilung/lehrende-aus-giessen-und-marburg-erhalten-ars-legendi-fakultaetenpreis|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She was named a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], in the 2022 class of fellows, "for contributions to differential geometry, in particular manifolds with special holonomy and on non-integrable geometric structures and for service to the mathematical community".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2022 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=5 November 2021}}</ref>
